properties.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

EDOUARD BECOMING BETTER ORGANIZED AS IT APPROACHES THE COAST NEAR THE TEXAS
AND LOUISIANA BORDER.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Southern Liberty

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Chambers, and Southern Liberty

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 120 miles east of Galveston TX
- 29.0N 92.8W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 300 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard is showing signs of strengthening as it
approaches the Upper Texas Coast. The system's outer rainbands are
already reaching the coastline near High Island and Galveston. These
rainbands will continue to push into our southeastern coastal counties
this morning, before pushing farther inland this afternoon and evening.
The system is forecast to become a strong tropical storm before moving
ashore near Sabine, TX early this afternoon. The primary concern for
our area will be heavy rainfall. The heaviest showers and thunderstorms
could produce 3-4" per hour rainfall rates, which would result in
flash flooding. Worth mentioning that residual tropical moisture could
result in scattered heavy showers and thunderstorms on Wednesday as well.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited but track dependent
- Potential for some tree damage within the Tropical Storm Warning area,
especially if the center deviates west of the track.
- Scattered power and communications outages are possible.


Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
No significant impacts from surge are expected.



* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across southeast Texas. Potential
impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Streams and bayous may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots and where heavy rainbands occur.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.



* TORNADOES:
Tornado threat appears to be very low at this time.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:


Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!


Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 10 AM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**Tropical Storm Edouard Expected To Strengthen Before Landfall This Afternoon**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning has been issued for Hardin, Northern
Orange, Southern Jasper, Southern Newton, Southern Orange, and
Upper Jefferson

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Warning, Tropical Storm Warning, and Hurricane
Watch are in effect for Lower Jefferson and West Cameron
- A Storm Surge Warning and Tropical Storm Warning are in effect
for East Cameron
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Hardin, Lower
Vermilion, Northern Orange, Southern Jasper, Southern Newton,
Southern Orange, and Upper Jefferson

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 60 miles south-southeast of Cameron LA or about 110 miles
west-southwest of Morgan City LA
- 29.0N 92.8W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 300 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard continues to track west-northwest offshore of
the southwest Louisiana coast toward coastal southeast Texas or
extreme southwest Louisiana while becoming better organized. Tropical
Storm Warnings remain in effect for Vermilion and Cameron Parishes
including Calcasieu and Sabine Lakes as well as Jefferson, Orange,
Hardin, southern Jasper, and southern Newton Counties in Texas. To
account for any intensification prior to landfall, a Hurricane Watch
has been added for Jefferson County in Texas and western Cameron
Parish, east of Calcasieu Pass in Louisiana. Very breezy conditions
may also occur in Calcasieu Parish as well as Tyler, northern
Newton, and northern Jasper Counties. A Storm Surge Warning is now
in effect from High Island, Tx to Cameron, LA accounting 3 to 5
feet, while east of Cameron to Vermilion / Cameron Parish line
accounts for 1 to 3 feet. The forecast track remains largely
unchanged with a landfall expected near or west of Sabine, TX.
Flooding rainfall threat remains primarily along the coastal
parishes in southwest Louisiana and into Southeast Texas.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* SURGE:
Protect against life-threatening surge having possible significant
impacts across coastal Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf breaching dunes. Strong and
numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

Also, protect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited
impacts across South Central Louisiana.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Southeast Texas and Southwest Louisiana. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible
significant impacts across Southeast Texas and Southwest Louisiana.
Potential impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across south central Louisiana.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Storm surge is the leading killer associated with tropical storms and
hurricanes! Make sure you are in a safe area away from the surge
zone. Even if you are not in a surge-prone area, you could find
yourself cutoff by flood waters during and after the storm. Heed
evacuation orders issued by the local authorities.

Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. If you are in a flood-prone
area, consider moving to higher ground. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

-----------

Service in Lake Charles LA around 10 AM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 1 at 5:26PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A large and disorganized tropical disturbance is located east-
northeast of the Marianas and is producing isolated to numerous,
locally heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms. This system is
expected to move through or just north of the Marianas over the next
two days. A col has developed over the Marianas between this
disturbance and another system to the northwest. This will keep winds
fairly light through Wednesday. The unstable airmass and high
precipitable water values may allow for heavy showers to develop and
stall over the islands, creating a potential flooding risk. However,
high uncertainty remains in where the highest rainfall amounts will
occur and there may be breaks between instances of heavy rainfall.

By Thursday, a monsoonal tail may develop and push north into the
Marianas, bringing more locally heavy showers and isolated
thunderstorms, with the highest chances remaining over Guam and
Rota. Sustained winds of 15 to 25 mph will be possible with gusts of
30 mph.

HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

**Tropical Storm Edouard Expected To Strengthen Before Landfall On
Tuesday**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- The Storm Surge Watch has been upgraded to a Storm Surge
Warning and a Hurricane Watch have been issued for Lower
Jefferson and West Cameron
- The Storm Surge Watch has been upgraded to a Storm Surge
Warning for East Cameron

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Warning, Tropical Storm Warning, and Hurricane
Watch are in effect for Lower Jefferson and West Cameron
- A Storm Surge Warning and Tropical Storm Warning are in effect
for East Cameron
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Lower Vermilion

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 170 miles east-southeast of High Island TX or about 120
miles southeast of Cameron LA
- 28.6N 91.8W
- Storm Intensity 40 mph
- Movement West-northwest or 300 degrees at 7 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Edouard continues to track west-northwest offshore of
the central Louisiana Coast toward coastal Southeast Texas. The storm
is located about 140 miles Southeast of Lake Charles, LA. Tropical
Storm Warnings remain in effect for Vermilion and Cameron Parishes
including Calcasieu and Sabine Lakes as well as Jefferson County,
Texas. To account for any intensification prior to landfall, a
Hurricane Watch has been added for Jefferson County in Texas and
western Cameron Parish, east of Calcasieu Pass in Louisiana. A Storm
Surge Warning is now in effect from High Island, Tx to Cameron, LA
accounting 3 to 5 feet, while east of Cameron to Vermilion / Cameron
Parish line accounts for 1 to 3 feet. The forecast track remains
largely unchanged with a landfall expected near or west of Sabine, TX.
Flooding rainfall threat remain primarily along the coastal Parishes
and counties west from the Lower Atchafalaya extending northwest across
extreme Southwest Louisiana and into Southeast Texas as Edouard
attempts to build / maintain convection on the northern semi-circle.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* SURGE:
Protect against life-threatening surge having possible significant
impacts across coastal Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas.
Potential impacts in this area include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf breaching dunes. Strong and
numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

Also, protect against locally hazardous surge having possible limited
impacts across South Central Louisiana.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across far Southwest Louisiana into Southeast Texas.
Potential impacts include:
- Moderate rainfall flooding may prompt several evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly become swollen with swifter
currents and overspill their banks in a few places, especially
in usually vulnerable spots. Small streams, creeks, canals, and
ditches overflow.
- Flood waters can enter some structures or weaken foundations.
Several places may experience expanded areas of rapid
inundation at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Some streets and parking lots take on moving water as
storm drains and retention ponds overflow. Driving conditions
become hazardous. Some road and bridge closures.

Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across south-central Louisiana.

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
Southeast Texas and Southwest Louisiana. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:

Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

Storm surge is the leading killer associated with tropical storms and
hurricanes! Make sure you are in a safe area away from the surge
zone. Even if you are not in a surge-prone area, you could find
yourself cutoff by flood waters during and after the storm. Heed
evacuation orders issued by the local authorities.

Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. If you are in a flood-prone
area, consider moving to higher ground. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Lake Charles LA around 4 AM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

Quality Alert for the Kansas City metropolitan area, with ground
level ozone being the primary pollutant from 9 AM to 7 PM CDT
Tuesday.

Members of sensitive groups may experience health effects.

People and businesses are urged to avoid activities which lead to
ozone formation. These activities include refueling vehicles or
topping off when refueling idling vehicles unnecessarily and using
gasoline powered lawn equipment. Positive activities include car
pooling, biking to work, delaying or combining errands, and using
water-based paints and cleaners.

When pollution levels are elevated, the Mid-America Regional Council
recommends that individuals consider limiting strenuous outdoor
physical activity to reduce the risk of adverse health effects.
People who may be especially sensitive to the effects of elevated
levels of pollutants include the very young and those with
preexisting respiratory problems such as asthma or heart disease.
Those with symptoms should consider consulting their personal
physician.

For further information, please see the Mid-America Regional Council
air quality program website at http://www.airqkc.org.
